Each package keeps its own changelog. This page is a pointer, not a copy — a
mirrored changelog goes stale the first time a release happens without a site
rebuild.

## Current versions

Rather than a table that drifts, check what you actually have installed:

``` r
vapply(c("splitGraph", "bioLeak", "fastml"),
       function(p) as.character(utils::packageVersion(p)),
       character(1))
```

and what CRAN currently has:

``` r
available <- utils::available.packages()
available[c("splitGraph", "bioLeak", "fastml"), "Version"]
```

## Compatibility

The cross-package seams are narrow on purpose, which is what keeps them stable:

- **splitGraph → anything.** The `split_spec` contract is versioned, and
  `migrate_json()` handles older serialisations. A contract test in splitGraph
  pins the fields a consumer may rely on.
- **bioLeak → tidymodels.** `as_rsample()` produces a standard `rset`. Anything
  that accepts an `rset` accepts bioLeak folds, including `fastml(resamples = )`.

If a release breaks either seam, it will say so in that package's NEWS under a
breaking-change heading.

## Reporting problems

Report against the package where the behaviour occurs:

- [splitGraph issues](https://github.com/selcukorkmaz/splitGraph/issues)
- [bioLeak issues](https://github.com/selcukorkmaz/bioLeak/issues)
- [fastml issues](https://github.com/selcukorkmaz/fastml/issues)

For something that only shows up when two packages are combined, open it against
the *downstream* one — the package that consumed the object — and link the
upstream call that produced it.
